title: THE FREQUENCY THAT KNOWS TOMORROW - Part 1: The Voice on the Radio
notes: Qwen3-TTS. 'radio' and 'phone' are YOUR voice (same designed voice) with radio / phone colouring applied per line (fx). Run narrate with ~/.venvs/qwentts/bin/python ... --engine qwen.

narrator.design: Male narrator, late 30s, low calm baritone, quiet late-night storytelling voice, slight rasp, unhurried.

you.design: Young man, early 20s, warm late-night radio host voice, friendly mid-low tone, clear diction, a little tired.
you.ref_text: You're listening to the late show. It's just you and me tonight, so stay with me, and keep the lights on.

unknown.design: Older man, 60s, low and slow, gentle in a wrong way, too friendly, slightly hoarse, very close to the phone.
unknown.ref_text: Hello there. I didn't mean to scare you. I just wanted to know if anyone was still awake in there.

lines.text: Your radio station just played a recording of you dying.
The recording was made ninety seconds from now.
You're working alone during the night shift.
It's one-oh-six AM.
Suddenly, the studio speakers turn on by themselves.
Then you hear your own voice.
"If you're hearing this, don't answer line three."
You check the recording. There's no file.
No scheduled broadcast. Nothing.
Then the studio phone starts ringing.
Line three. You stare at it.
The phone's cable is lying disconnected on the floor.
The recording starts playing again.
This time, your voice sounds terrified.
"Whatever you do... don't let him know you're alone!"
The phone stops ringing. Silence.
Then someone speaks through the receiver.
"Hello? Are you alone in there?"
You slowly step away from the phone.
The speakers suddenly crackle. Your own voice returns.
"You answered him last time. You just don't remember."
You freeze. The recording continues.
"You have to destroy the transmitter."
Suddenly, the studio computer displays a new message.
Transmission received. The sender? Your own radio station.
The message reads: stop listening to the version of you that wants to survive.
Then the phone rings again. This time, the voice on the receiver is yours.
"Please. Don't destroy the transmitter."
You have two conflicting warnings.
One version of you says destroy the transmitter. Another begs you to keep it running.
"Whatever you choose... one of us is going to disappear tonight."
Comment A or B. Your choice decides Part 2.
